supporting_observations.claim: At 13:50:51 UTC, WS-JFROST-01 sent 51,000,438 bytes to the explicit proxy at 10.53.20.30:8080 over a connection lasting about 17 seconds; the connection reports 8,929 bytes in the reverse direction.

The logged connection establishes a large transfer from the workstation to the proxy, but does not identify the ultimate destination or show what data was transferred. The available record alone therefore does not establish that the bytes reached an external destination or were malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available Zeek HTTP record contains byte counts and connection metadata but no URL, HTTP method, hostname, content, or proxy disposition.
No proxy access logs, endpoint process attribution, or file-access evidence for the large transfer are provided.
The alert describes activity around 13:46 UTC, while the supplied large-transfer record is timestamped 13:50:51 UTC; the evidence does not explain that timing difference.
claims_not_established: Whether the transfer was an upload to an external service or otherwise terminated at the proxy.
The destination service, account, URL, and purpose of the transfer.
Whether the transferred data contained confidential or otherwise sensitive information.
Which process and interactive user initiated the transfer, and whether it was authorized.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve PROXY-MAP-01 access logs for the connection, including destination host, URL, method, authenticated user, and response or policy action.
Correlate WS-JFROST-01 endpoint network telemetry with process and user attribution at 13:50:51 UTC.
Check endpoint file-access and application records around the transfer to identify any file or data staged or sent.
Confirm with the workstation user or relevant business owner whether a transfer of this size was expected and authorized.
unrelated_findings: At 14:18:50 UTC, WmiPrvSE.exe on WS-JFROST-01 accessed svchost.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1400. This is outside the alerted transfer and should be triaged separately; the supplied record does not establish maliciousness. (T149-00265)
